name: Comma API
description:
REST API for Comma (commareports.com): publish HTML reports, edit them in place with full revision history, comment with anchors, share, attach assets, run AI reviewers, and schedule regeneration with routines, skills, and connectors.

**Authentication.** Every endpoint (except this spec) takes a Comma personal API token as `Authorization: Bearer comma_sk_…`. Tokens are minted in Settings → API tokens, carry granular scopes (`reports:read`, `reports:write`, `comments:read`, `comments:write`, `routines`, `connections`, `sharing`; `*` = full access), can expire, and are revocable. Each operation below lists the scope it requires.

**Rate limits.** Rate limit: per-token sliding window (plan-aware — Free 60 req/min, Pro 600, Team/Enterprise 6000 by default); 429 responses carry a Retry-After header.

**Errors.** Errors are JSON: `{ "error": "…" }` — 401 bad/missing token, 403 missing scope or no access to the resource, 404 not found (also used instead of 403 where existence must not leak), 429 rate limited.

**MCP mirror.** The Model Context Protocol server at `https://commareports.com/api/mcp` (Streamable HTTP transport) exposes this same surface as tools (`create_report`, `add_comment`, `run_routine`, …) for Claude Code, Cursor, and VS Code. It authenticates with the same `comma_sk_…` Bearer token, and scope, revocation, expiry, and rate limiting behave identically across both transports.

A handful of operations (`/skills*`, `/connectors*`, `/routines/{id}/run`, `/me/*`) alternatively accept a signed-in Supabase user-session JWT as the Bearer token — that is the browser UI's path; agents should always use `comma_sk_…` tokens.
